chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Abu Abdillah al-Abzari said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot and prayed the two rak'at of the obligatory Tawaf in the Hijr.
He said: 'He should repeat them behind the Maqam, because Allah the Exalted says, "And take you the Maqam of Ibrahim as a place of prayer," meaning thereby the two rak'at of the obligatory Tawaf.'

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two rak'at of prayer performed as part of the obligatory circumambulation
key_terms.فِي الْحِجْرِ: In the Hijr (the semi-circular wall area adjacent to the Kaaba)
key_terms.مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The Station of Abraham, a stone in the Masjid al-Haram

ai.seo_question: Where should one repeat the two rak'at of Tawaf if they were prayed in the Hijr by mistake?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *nasi* (forgetfulness) regarding the two rak'at of Tawaf, emphasizing the sanctity of the Maqam Ibrahim as the designated prayer spot. The Imam’s citation of the Quranic verse not only provides the legal basis for the location but also highlights the theological link between the physical station and the ritual act of prayer, a point of emphasis in Shia juristic discussions on the Kaaba's architecture.
